The '''2012–13 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team''' represented [[North Carolina State University]] in the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team's head coach was [[Mark Gottfried]] in his second season. The team played their home games at [[PNC Arena]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]], as a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 24–11, 11–7 in ACC play to finish in a tie for fourth place. They advanced to the semifinals of the [[2013 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] where they lost to Miami (FL). They received an at-large bid to the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the second round to Temple.

==Preseason==
National pundits talked a lot about the Wolfpack in their early preseason discussions of the top teams in the country. NC State returned its top four leading scorers from the 2011-12 season in [[C. J. Leslie]] (14.7 ppg), [[Lorenzo Brown]] (12.7 ppg), Scott Wood (12.4 ppg) and [[Richard Howell (basketball)|Richard Howell]] (10.8 ppg). In addition, NC State landed Rodney Purvis, Tyler Lewis, and [[T. J. Warren]] to wrap up a Top 10 recruiting class. ESPN’s [[Andy Katz]] had the Wolfpack as the top rated ACC squad, at No. 6, in his early predictions.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7767401/indiana-hoosiers-continue-moving-2012-13 |title=Rebuilt Hoosiers will join the elite |first=Andy |last=Katz |author-link=Andy Katz |work=ESPN.com |date=April 3, 2012 |accessdate=May 13, 2022}}</ref> His counterpart, Sports Illustrated’s Luke Winn, had the Wolfpack listed as the No. 5 team in the nation according to his power rankings.{{Citation needed|date=August 2013}} NC State was ranked 20th in the final ESPN/USA Today Coaches Poll following its Sweet Sixteen run in the NCAA Tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2012 |title=2011–12 Men's College Basketball Rankings for Final Rankings |work=ESPN.com |accessdate=May 13, 2022}}</ref>

==Schedule and results==
NC State's January 12 win over (AP) #1 Duke was the program's sixth win over an AP #1 program and their second over Duke as the AP #1 team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/152/north-carolina-state-wolfpack|title = NC State Wolfpack College Basketball - NC State News, Scores, Stats, Rumors & More - ESPN}}</ref>  NC State's last win over an AP #1 team was Feb. 15, 2004, also over Duke.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/_/id/152/north-carolina-state-wolfpack|title = NC State Wolfpack College Basketball - NC State News, Scores, Stats, Rumors & More - ESPN}}</ref>  [[ESPN]]'s [[College GameDay (basketball)|College GameDay]] covered the January 26th game against UNC, marking the first and only time that the Wolfpack have appeared on the basketball version of the program.<ref>{{Cite web|title = ESPN College GameDay Coming To Raleigh For UNC Vs. NC State On Jan. 26|url = http://www.backingthepack.com/2012/8/8/3228255/espn-college-gameday-schedule-nc-state-basketball|website = Backing The Pack|date = 8 August 2012|accessdate = 2015-08-06}}</ref>
